newsitem.title: BULGARIA: No deals struck in Bulgarian Zunk bonds auction.
newsitem.headline: No deals struck in Bulgarian Zunk bonds auction.

text.p: No deals were struck on the first Zunk bonds secondary auction held by the Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) due to lack of interest and excessive lev liquidity, traders said on Wednesday.

"The auction is late in time. It could have been done two-three months ago when the interest in Zunks was higher, liquidity was low and trade was much livelier," a dealer from a foreign bank local branch said.
Investors' interest in the bonds has been running high since March, when the new reformist government pledged to speed up privatisation. The bonds are accepted as means of payment in local sell-offs.
Financial institutions have so far traded lev- and dollar denominated Zunks on bilateral basis.
Tuesday's auction offered an issue of lev-denominated Zunks with par value of 19.813 billion levs at end-May, and dollar-denominated Zunks with par of $917.6 million.

Bids amounted to 7.770 billion levs for issue 98/93 of lev-denominated Zunk bonds with no offers. The minimum price of the bids was 570 percent of par and the maximum was 685 percent of par, the BNB said in a statement.

Bids for $13.28 million and offers for $3 million of the dollar-denominated Zunks issue numbered 97/94 were placed but no deals were struck as the highest bid was 69 percent of par and the lowest of the offers stood at 70 percent.
"We have plenty of levs now and do not need to sell any paper at this moment," one trader said.
Other traders said they had permanent clients with whom they traded directly.
The short notice and the BNB requirement for banks to place only one bid on behalf of a client also curbed participation in the auction, the trader added.
"We received the auction announcement late on Friday and had no time to negotiate with all our clients and place a wider price margin," a trader said.
The Zunks' secondary auctions could become an indicator of their market value when deals are struck at an equilibrum price, traders said.

Only financial institutions that are primary dealers of government securities were allowed to take part in the auction with 12 out of 28 taking part. Participants in the auction could place only one order on their behalf and one order on behalf of their clients.
